findings.text: Someone arriving at the Athena site URL never learns what Athena is. The page names only "the study" and a footer path, and nothing says who or what produced the study, or why.
findings.source: <title>How firstmate handles work</title>; "A reading of firstmate at one pinned commit, from the study firstmate-work-handling."

findings.text: This part works. Three short bullets and a six-step walk-through let a newcomer say what firstmate does and follow one item from Queued to Done.
findings.source: Start here > What firstmate is: "Firstmate takes an item from a backlog and gives it to a worker, which does the work in its own isolated worktree"

findings.text: The page never says why firstmate or this study matters, or who should care. It never says what a reader might use firstmate for, or what problem the study answers.
findings.source: Start here: "The three parts below say what it is, follow one piece of work, and define the words the rest of the page uses."

findings.text: There is no next step. The repository appears only as plain code text, not a link, and nothing says to install, read the source, or see other studies. The claim sources such as "AGENTS.md:206-206" are not linked either.
Some key terms stay unclear. The glossary never says whether the captain is a human user. "Home" is used in the glossary and in claims c1 and c15 but is never defined.
findings.source: Glossary: "captain — The one who approves merges and local-only landings when yolo is off."; c1: "refuses when this home has no item for the work"

findings.text: Guards marked "none (checked by agent)" in t5, t7 and t8 contradict themselves. The explanation comes only at the end, in Limits finding f2, and uses internal field names such as "guard_evaluated_by" that mean nothing to a newcomer.
findings.source: Transitions, t5: "Guard: none (checked by agent)"; Limits f2: "These transitions carry agent there as a placeholder"

findings.text: This sentence is awkward and describes the page's layout instead of the content. Glossary entries tagged "about this page" (state, transition, claim, pin, mark) add more page-about-page material before the content.
findings.source: Transitions lead-in: "The two deciders are explained below the cards' heading."

findings.text: The page is honest that the study comes only from reading the code. That helps a careful reader judge how much to trust it.
findings.source: Limits of this study, f1: "no failure or retry edge was observed; every claim is marked read"
